review-resolved-specification.Message: The resolved specification faithfully carries the original requirement forward and correctly incorporates the human decision (Unicode-aware char.IsLetterOrDigit-based classification) into both the normative Requirements and the AcceptanceCriteria, including two accented-letter examples (café, naïve) that were independently re-derived and confirmed correct. All 16 acceptance criteria were independently recomputed against the stated word definition and match the specified expected values; no contradictions between requirements, examples, and definitions were found, and no corrupted/replacement-character literals (e.g., U+FFFD) were detected. Remaining issues are non-blocking: a decision-ID citation mismatch, one OpenQuestion (apostrophes) that is actually already resolved by the base definition and should be promoted into the normative text, and two testability gaps where the broadened Unicode claim (non-Latin scripts, non-ASCII digits, and the resulting CJK single-word-run behavior) is asserted but not covered by any acceptance criterion, plus a lingering ambiguity around supplementary-plane (surrogate pair) handling that is already tracked as an open question. None of these block downstream test generation for the currently specified ASCII/BMP-Latin cases, but the omissions should be closed before claiming full Unicode coverage is verified.
